title: research-lab-standup-sprintnotes-sep07-2026
content:
Weekly applied-ML research notes — sprint starting 2026-09-07

Quick context:
- Focus this week: wrap up initial quantization quality sweep for the 13B family, validate KV-cache interactions, and triage regressions surfaced by the nightly evals. Also continued work on onboarding the new Falcon-like model variant into the serving catalog (model-onboard-NEBULA).
- Meeting cadence: M/W/F standups + Tue deep-dive. Notes below are captured from standups, bench runs, and pairing sessions. Informal / WIP.

Attendees (regular): Asha, Diego, Hannah, Jonah; occasional: Priya (SRE), Mateo (serving-runtime)

Major outcomes and decisions:
- Decided to freeze quant config set Qv2 for broader A/B evaluation: 4-bit asymmetric per-channel, GPTQ-like group-size 128, clip-healing enabled. Rationale: best tradeoff observed on devset for answer-fidelity vs token throughput.
- Rollout plan for Qv2: canary on 5% traffic for dedicated pools only; fallback to float16 variant on >2% error rate. Action: Jonah to add canary policy to rollout YAML by 2026-09-09 (JIRA-1439).
- KV-cache behavior: discovered ~1.8% token-accuracy drift when combining prefix caching with quantized FFN paths at sequence lengths >2048. Temporary mitigation: disable prefix-preserve caching for quantized instances until patch (see "open issues").

Experiment log (raw, reproducible commands and summary):
- Baseline (float16) model: nebula-13b-v1
  - eval: openqa-mini (2k samples), MRR: 0.842, EM: 0.72, avg latency P95: 210ms@1k tokens batch1
- Qv2 (our quant config) on nebula-13b-v1-quant:
  - eval: openqa-mini, MRR: 0.819 (-0.023), EM: 0.701 (-0.019)
  - latency: P95 110ms@1k tokens batch1 (approx 1.9x speedup)
  - token throughput: 2.1k tok/s vs 1.1k tok/s baseline
  - cost estimate: ~44% token inference cost reduction
  - notes: hallucination rate on closed-book QA increased for worst-case prompts; see example prompt id: qz-347.
- Variant test: Qv2 + group-size 64 (Qv2g64)
  - eval: MRR 0.826, EM 0.708 — slightly better than Qv2 but slower (1.6x speedup). Consider for latency-sensitive but quality-strict customers.

Nightly evals summary (auto-run 02:00 UTC):
- Regression spike detected 2026-09-08 for models matching pattern *nebula-*-quant on dataset openqa-mini and safety-checker: false positives increased by 0.6pp. Alert routed to #applied-ml; assignment: Diego to triage with eval harness (JIRA-1442).
- Root cause hypothesis: per-channel asymmetric quantization combo with layernorm scaling at inference-time -> numeric corner cases for low-prob tokens.

Open issues / TODOs:
- KV-cache + quant interaction (priority HIGH): reproduce locally with minimal repro script and file issue in runtime repo. Owner: Hannah. Target: 2026-09-11.
- Add targeted eval dataset for code-heavy prompts (CodeQA-1000) to catch regressions in model-onboard NEBULA (owner: Jonah).
- Formalize canary rollback thresholds in Redwood Console: define explicit error budget and automated rollback triggers for model-quality regressions (owner: Asha).
- Investigate hallucination examples (sample ids attached in linked_artifacts). Diego to produce 10 curated examples and suggested root-cause notes.

Implementation notes and snippets (copied from pairing session):
- Local repro (python):
  - python -m rwinf.eval --model nebula-13b-v1-quant --dataset datasets/openqa-mini --batch-size 1 --max-tokens 1024 --kv-cache True --quant-config qv2
- Canary rollout YAML snippet (work-in-progress):
  - route: dedicated
  - canary_percent: 5
  - fallback: nebula-13b-v1-fp16
  - eval-monitor: nightly-openqa-mini
- Experiment infra: use bench-runner v0.27 (docker tag: rwinf/bench:v0.27) — fixes docker memory leak from v0.26 that skewed latency P95.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Try hybrid strategy: store attention keys in float16 KV-cache but quantize FFN weights (might reduce drift). Could be a good middle-ground for latency for seq>1k.
- Consider automated ``prompt-slicing'' eval to identify prompts that are sensitive to quantization (short-list candidate prompts for human review).

Meeting snippets (raw):
- Jonah: "If we can get Qv2g64 into dedicated pools we can advertise 30–40% lower unit costs for latency-sensitive tiers."
- Priya (SRE): "If you disable prefix-preserve, we should communicate impact to customers; also make sure autoscaling policy accounts for extra compute with full-cache fallbacks."

Files & PRs to review this week:
- gh:repo/model-quant-prs#58 — patch to clip-healing implementation. Review by 2026-09-09 (Asha assigned).
- gh:repo/serving-runtime#402 — KV-cache numeric edge-case fix (in review, Mateo).
- Confluence: quant-onboarding-checklist — add step for safety/regression evaluation for code-capable prompts.

Wrap-up / next steps for next standup (2026-09-09):
- Jonah: complete canary rollout yaml + smoke test in staging.
- Diego: produce curated hallucination examples + start JIRA triage.
- Hannah: minimal repro for KV-cache + quant interaction.
- Asha: draft short customer-facing note for early access users (if canary goes live) and update experiments table in Confluence.

Misc / scratchpad (short form):
- slack: search "qtz-nebula" channel for customer reports (2 threads)
- linear: create card for "add CodeQA-1000 to nightly evals"
- question: do we need a separate quantized model fingerprint (hash + quant-config) in the model-catalog? probably yes — attach to onboarding checklist.

End of notes.

(This doc is intentionally informal; will extract a cleaner exec summary if/when we approve canary rollout.)
